newsitem.title: HONG KONG: New Zealand recognises future Hong Kong passport.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand recognises future Hong Kong passport.

text.p: New Zealand has announced that it will recognise the passports that Hong Kong will issue after the territory reverts to China on July 1, a Hong Kong government spokesman said on Wednesday.

New Zealand will treat passports of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, which the territory will be called from July 1, the same as it now treats the British National Overseas (BNO) passport, he said.
BNO passport holders need a visa to enter New Zealand.
The Hong Kong government welcomed New Zealand's decision and said in a statement it would continue with the current practise of allowing New Zealanders a visa-free stay for up to three months.

A string of countries including Britain, the United States, Canada, Singapore, Japan, the Philippines and Western Samoa have recognised the territory's post-handover passport and announced favourable entry conditions ranging from easy visas to visa-free access.
